newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: FORECAST-S.Africa April CPI seen hitting year peak.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-S.Africa April CPI seen hitting year peak.

text.p: South African financial markets can look forward to a positive set of economic figures over the next fortnight after a rollercoaster ride this week, economists said on Friday.
The April trade balance is expected in the second half of next week, but the more closely watched figure will be the consumer inflation number.
Most economists expected the April consumer price index next week, but the Central Statistical Service (CSS) said on Friday the number was due out only in the week starting May 26.

A Reuters consensus poll of nine economists forecast the consumer price index would remain flat from the March figure at 0.6 percent month-on-month or 9.6 percent year-on-year when inflation dipped for the first time in 11 months.

"The good news is that the April figure should either confirm that the 9.8 percent (year-on-year rise) in February was the peak or that, if the figure surprises on the high side, that will represent the peak," said Rand Merchant Bank treasury economist Julia Roy.
The monthly pace of increasing food prices was starting to moderate and the benefits of lower imported inflation due to the rand's appreciation this year should start flowing through, Roy said.
Sandra Gordon of Syfrets saw a peak of 0.8 percent month-on-month or 9.8 percent year-on-year in April with inflation expected to taper off to around 9.4 percent in May.
The unfavourable prospect of double digit inflation -- anticipated at the start of the year -- was fast receding, economists agreed, with inflation seen edging lower after the April number.
Factors seen putting pressure on inflation in April included increased taxes on tobacco and alcohol introduced in the March budget and a low base factor from a year ago.

"Normally the April number can be a bit of a jump and last April happened to be quite low so there is potential for the index to move up a bit," said Kevin Lings of Nedcor, forecasting a year-on-year rise above consensus at 9.9 percent or 0.9 percent month-on-month.
But he agreed April would likely represent the peak in consumer inflation, although producer inflation could still peak beyond the consumer figure, possibly above ten percent.
Producer price inflation rose to a 21-month high of 0.1 percent or 9.6 percent in March after rising 9.3 percent in February.

Most economists again shied away from forecasting a number for the traditionally volatile trade figure, but generally looked for an improving performance on the back of healthier export growth relative to that of imports.
Those brave enough to stick out their necks expected another surplus of around 900 million rand after a 1.98 billion surplus in March and from a 451.6 million deficit in February.
"On an average type basis the performance is looking quite good with expectations of imports easing and exports doing a bit better," Nedcor's Lings said.

Others searching their crystal balls expected an on-going improvement on a rolling three-month basis with the pace of export growth picking up relative to that of imports, restoring confidence in a substantially reduced 1997 current account deficit.
South African first quarter GDP growth figures are expected out towards the end of the month but this still has to be confirmed by the CSS.
